parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Solid manganese(IV) oxide, $\text{MnO}_2$, catalyses the decomposition of hydrogen peroxide.

$$2\text{H}_2\text{O}_2\text{(aq)} \rightarrow 2\text{H}_2\text{O}\text{(l)} + \text{O}_2\text{(g)}$$

State the type of catalysis for this reaction. Explain your answer.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem:
Hydrogen peroxide reacts with iodide ions in acidic conditions as shown.

$$\text{H}_2\text{O}_2 + 2\text{I}^- + 2\text{H}^+ \rightarrow 2\text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{I}_2$$

The initial rate of this reaction is investigated with different concentrations of $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$, $\text{I}^-$ and $\text{H}^+$. The results obtained are shown in Table 3.1.

Table 3.1

| experiment | $[\text{H}_2\text{O}_2]/\text{mol dm}^{-3}$ | $[\text{I}^-]/\text{mol dm}^{-3}$ | $[\text{H}^+]/\text{mol dm}^{-3}$ | initial rate/$\text{mol dm}^{-3}\text{s}^{-1}$ |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | 0.0450 | 0.0300 | 0.0125 | $2.42 \times 10^{-3}$ |
| 2 | 0.0225 | 0.0600 | 0.0125 | $2.42 \times 10^{-3}$ |
| 3 | 0.0225 | 0.120 | 0.0125 | $4.84 \times 10^{-3}$ |
| 4 | 0.0450 | 0.120 | 0.0500 | $9.68 \times 10^{-3}$ |
parts.text:
Use the information in Table 3.1 to deduce the rate equation for this reaction.

Explain your reasoning.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Use your rate equation from (b)(i) and the data from Experiment 1 to calculate the rate constant, $k$, for this reaction. Include the units of $k$.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem:
The rate of the thermal decomposition of azomethane, $\text{CH}_3\text{N=NCH}_3$, is investigated.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{N=NCH}_3 \rightarrow \text{N}_2 + \text{C}_2\text{H}_6$$

Fig. 3.1 shows the results obtained. The reaction is first order with respect to $\text{CH}_3\text{N=NCH}_3$.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

Fig. 3.1
parts.text: Use Fig. 3.1 to calculate **two** half-lives, $t_{\frac{1}{2}}$, to show that the reaction is first order.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Use your answer to (c)(i) to calculate the rate constant, $k$, for the decomposition of azomethane.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Describe the effect of increasing temperature on the rate constant and on the rate of a reaction.
